[id="file-citation-annotation-reference_{context}"]
= File citation annotation reference

[role="_abstract"]
The `file_citation` annotation type is returned by Llama Stack through the OpenAI-compatible Responses API.
You can use this information to parse and display citation data in your application.

ifndef::upstream[]
[IMPORTANT]
====

[id="annotation-location_{context}"]
== Annotation location

Annotations are returned in the `annotations` field of `output_text` content items within the `output[].content[]` structure of the Responses API response.

The following example shows a complete Responses API response payload that includes file citation annotations.
When the `file_search` tool is used, the `output` array contains a `file_search_call` item followed by a `message` item.
The annotations appear in the `content` array of the `message` item.

[source,json]
----
{
  "id": "resp-abc123",
  "object": "response",
  "created_at": 1749638400,
  "model": "meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct",
  "output": [
    {
      "type": "file_search_call",
      "id": "fs_abc123",
      "status": "completed",
      "queries": [
        "Red Bank Financial overview"
      ],
      "results": null
    },
    {
      "type": "message",
      "id": "msg_abc123",
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": [
        {
          "type": "output_text",
          "text": "According to the document, Red Bank Financial is a community-focused financial institution.",
          "annotations": [
            {
              "type": "file_citation",
              "file_id": "file-57610eaac6364459bfefae60377837b7",
              "filename": "redbankfinancial_about.pdf",
              "index": 139
            },
            {
              "type": "file_citation",
              "file_id": "file-a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6",
              "filename": "redbankfinancial_services.pdf",
              "index": 42
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "status": "completed"
}
----

[NOTE]
====
When the `include` parameter is set to `file_search_call.results` in the request, the `file_search_call` item contains a `results` array with extended search result metadata.
When `include` is not specified, the `results` field is `null`.
====

[id="supported-annotation-type_{context}"]
== Supported annotation type

In {productname-short}, Llama Stack returns the `file_citation` annotation type when using the `file_search` tool.

[id="openai-annotation-type-compatibility_{context}"]
== OpenAI annotation type compatibility

The following table compares the annotation types defined in the OpenAI schema with their support status in Llama Stack in {productname-short} {vernum}.
The request schema for `file_search` tool configuration, including the `vector_store_ids` parameter, is identical to the OpenAI specification.

[cols="2,1,3",options="header"]
|===
|Annotation type |Status |Notes

|`file_citation`
|Supported
|Returned when the `file_search` tool retrieves content from a vector store.
Includes `file_id`, `filename`, and `index` fields.

|`url_citation`
|Not produced
|Defined in the OpenAI schema for web search results.
Llama Stack does not produce this type because it does not perform web searches.

|`container_file_citation`
|Not produced
|Defined in the OpenAI schema for container-based file retrieval.
This type is specific to OpenAI container environments.

|`file_path`
|Not produced
|Defined in the OpenAI schema for Code Interpreter file outputs.
Llama Stack does not include a Code Interpreter tool.
|===

[id="file-citation-fields_{context}"]
== File citation fields

The `file_citation` annotation includes the following fields:

[cols="1,1,2",options="header"]
|===
|Field |Type |Description

|type
|string
|Always `file_citation`.

|file_id
|string
|Identifier of the source file used during retrieval.

|filename
|string
|Name of the source file.

|index
|integer
|Character position in the output text where the citation should be inserted.
This value corresponds to the position in the generated text, not an index into a list of files.
|===

[NOTE]
====
Confidence scores are not included in file citation annotations.
The annotation provides document-level attribution without a relevance or confidence indicator.
====

[id="metadata-availability-by-pipeline-stage_{context}"]
== Metadata availability by pipeline stage

The following table shows which metadata fields are available at each stage of the retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline.
Custom attributes that you attach during file ingestion are preserved in search results but are not included in the final annotation output.

[cols="2,1,1,1",options="header"]
|===
|Metadata field |Vector store |Search results |File citation annotations

|`file_id`
|Yes
|Yes
|Yes

|`filename`
|Yes
|Yes
|Yes

|Custom attributes (for example, `title`, `author`)
|Yes
|Yes
|No

|Relevance score
|No
|Yes
|No

|Chunk text
|No
|Yes
|No

|`index`
|No
|No
|Yes

|Timestamps (created, modified)
|No
|No
|No

|Content type
|No
|No
|No
|===

To access search result metadata that is not included in annotations, use the `include` parameter with the value `file_search_call.results` in your Responses API request.
For more information, see xref:viewing-file-citation-annotations-in-responses-api-output_{context}[].

[id="annotation-behavior_{context}"]
== Annotation behavior

* Llama Stack attributes citations at the document level.
* Multiple annotations can reference the same index position.
* Chunk-level and token-level attribution are not supported.
* Annotations follow the OpenAI response schema without modification.

[id="ui-display-behavior_{context}"]
== UI display behavior

In the Llama Stack UI, file citation annotations display the source filename in the response output.
You can click the filename to download the corresponding source file.

The UI displays only the filename.
The `file_id` and `index` fields are accessible only through the API.
For more information about viewing annotations in the UI, see xref:viewing-file-citation-annotations-in-llama-stack-ui_{context}[].
